channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Two Teenagers Die in School Fights in Kyrgyzstan's Jalal-Abad Region
item.description: Two teenagers died in separate fights in Kyrgyzstan's Jalal-Abad region within the first days of the new school year. Authorities are holding meetings and parent gatherings in response to the incidents. One 17-year-old died after being beaten, and a 15-year-old died following an assault by older students.

item.title: StoneX Group Eyes Expansion in Kyrgyzstan's Financial Market
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov met with StoneX Group management in New York to discuss expanding cooperation. The company, which already partners with Kyrgyzstan on precious metals trading, expressed interest in leveraging its financial infrastructure for new projects in the country. Japarov highlighted Kyrgyzstan's desire to attract U.S. investment and expertise.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Seizes Over 101,000 Meters of Fishing Nets in Eight Months
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Natural Resources seized over 101,250 meters of synthetic fishing nets and removed 1,910 kilograms of trash from water bodies in the first eight months of 2026. The Toktogul Reservoir saw the largest seizure with 42,250 meters of nets. Issyk-Kul Lake and Son-Kul Lake also had significant amounts of nets removed.

item.title: 81st Session of UN General Assembly Opens in New York; Saida Mirziyoyeva Meets UN Secretary-General
item.description: The 81st session of the UN General Assembly has commenced in New York. Saida Mirziyoyeva met with UN Secretary-General António Guterres to discuss cooperation between Uzbekistan and the UN. Guterres expressed gratitude for Uzbekistan's support.

item.title: Gaza Students Return to In-Person Learning After Three Years Amidst War
item.description: Gaza students have returned to offline education after three years, despite 98% of schools being destroyed during the conflict with Israel. The Ministry of Education, with international support, launched the 2026/27 academic year, with classes held in damaged buildings and temporary tents.

item.title: Central Asian nations independently shape development priorities and cooperation formats, says Kramp-Karrenbauer
item.description: Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer, chair of the Konrad Adenauer Foundation, met with a Central Asian delegation in Italy. She noted the region's strategic importance and potential for growth, emphasizing that Central Asian countries are increasingly defining their own development priorities and practical cooperation formats.

item.title: Uzbek President congratulates Russian President on successful State Duma elections
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin on September 21. Mirziyoyev congratulated Putin on the successful State Duma elections and wished the new parliament fruitful work. They also discussed deepening strategic partnership and upcoming bilateral events.

item.title: Kyrgyz Lawmaker Questions Contradictory Healthcare Budget Data for 2025
item.description: MP Dastan Bekeshev expressed concern over contradictory data regarding Kyrgyzstan's 2025 healthcare budget, noting increased state spending alongside significant unused funds by the Compulsory Medical Insurance Fund. He highlighted issues like drug shortages and insufficient timely financing despite budget allocations.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliamentarian Proposes National Status for Osh Regional Hospital
item.description: Member of Parliament Bekmurza Ergeshov has proposed granting national status to the Osh Interregional United Clinical Hospital. The initiative, supported by the hospital's staff, aims to improve patient care. The hospital serves over 55,000 patients annually from three southern provinces and performs over 20,000 complex surgeries.

item.title: Uzbekistan Aims to Become Key Transport Hub Between Asia and Europe
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to double its transport services volume by 2030, attracting $9.1 billion in investments to become a key land route hub between Asia and Europe. The strategy includes expanding access to international markets. New airport complexes are under construction in Tashkent and Bukhara, with the Tashkent airport designed for 20 million passengers annually.

item.title: Roadworks on Balykchy-Bokonbaevo-Karakol highway are 95% complete
item.description: Asphalting work on the Balykchy-Bokonbaevo-Karakol highway is 95% complete, according to the Ministry of Transport and Communications. Sidewalks are being built and drainage pipes installed on various sections. The reconstruction of the 141.64 km road, which began in 2021, is funded by the cabinet of ministers with presidential support.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan to Cooperate on Drip Irrigation Systems
item.description: A Kyrgyz delegation visited Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan to discuss implementing drip and sprinkler irrigation. Memorandums of understanding were signed with companies in Almaty and Tashkent. These agreements aim to introduce water-saving technologies in Kyrgyzstan, improving water resource efficiency for agricultural lands.

item.title: Uzbekistan Declares Decade of National Rise, Prioritizing Education and Knowledge
item.description: Uzbekistan has declared the upcoming decade as an era of National Rise, emphasizing education and knowledge as key drivers of development. The first of seven national programs focuses on developing human capital by improving education from preschool to higher levels. The president stressed the crucial role of teachers in this national progress.

item.title: New poultry complex modernizes Karakalpakstan's food supply and economy
item.description: The "Kegeyli baraka naslli parranda" poultry complex in Karakalpakstan is a key modernization and import substitution project, costing $7.8 million. It now fully meets the region's demand for poultry meat and eggs, previously imported. The automated facility includes a feed mill and has created 70 jobs.

item.title: Central Asia regional integration stability discussed at Italy conference
item.description: Delegations from Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan met in Cadenabbia, Italy, to discuss strengthening Central Asia's regional integration. Discussions focused on making rapprochement sustainable, expanding public support, fostering trust, and building a common regional identity. Uzbekistan proposed the Fergana Peace Forum as a platform for trust-building.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economy Ministry Unveils Plan to Stabilize Prices Through 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Economy Ministry has presented a government plan for 2026-2027 to stabilize prices for goods and services. Measures include importing livestock and wheat, building warehouses, supporting farmers, and controlling fuel costs. The goal is to keep inflation between 7.7-8.5 percent in 2027.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Launch Pilot 'Green AI' Module for Agricultural Recommendations
item.description: Uzbekistan will pilot a 'Green AI' module to analyze soil composition, climate, and water supply in different regions. The system will provide recommendations on suitable areas and tree species for planting, optimizing agricultural practices.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prioritizes Combating Cybercrime and Raising Public Awareness
item.description: Uzbekistan is intensifying efforts against cybercrime, a key state policy priority. New measures aim to prevent and counter cyber threats, with a focus on educating citizens about cybersecurity. Scammers often use messaging apps, employing urgency and psychological pressure.

item.title: US Secretly Deported Over 25,000 Migrants to Third Countries
item.description: An investigation revealed that the US has deported over 25,000 migrants to third countries under secret agreements since Donald Trump took office. Approximately 20,000 were sent to Mexico, with others deported to 27 countries across Latin America, Africa, and Asia. Some deportees were sent to nations where they faced persecution.

item.title: Construction Company Fined in Bishkek for Safety Violations
item.description: A construction company in Bishkek was fined 200,000 soms for violating building codes and creating a safety hazard. Waste was dumped on adjacent territory, posing a risk to citizens. The company was ordered to rectify the violations within a set timeframe.

item.title: Uzbekistan Reasserts Role as Crossroads of Civilizations, Expert Says
item.description: An expert from Vienna University noted Uzbekistan's state visit to South Korea and the Central Asia-South Korea summit signify global geopolitical and economic shifts. He stated Tashkent is becoming a key economic and innovation driver in the region, reviving its historical mission as a bridge between East and West on a new technological level.

item.title: Anorbank Responds to Reports About Shareholder Kahramonjon Olimov
item.description: Anorbank stated that reports in foreign media about shareholder Kahramonjon Olimov are unrelated to the bank's capital, management, or operations. The bank clarified that these are personal matters of a shareholder and mixing them with bank activities is incorrect and unacceptable. Official confirmation of the alleged criminal case is pending.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Transport Ministry Proposes Digital System to Combat Shadow Economy
item.description: The shadow economy in Uzbekistan's freight transport sector exceeds 42 percent. The Ministry of Transport has proposed creating a unified digital transport system to legalize informal services. This initiative aims to establish a registry of carriers and an electronic system for orders and services, enhancing transparency and convenience.

item.title: Pakistan Strikes Three Targets in Afghanistan, Claims 28 'Terrorists' Eliminated
item.description: Pakistan announced it struck three targets in Afghanistan, eliminating 28 "terrorists." Islamabad stated the attacks targeted "terrorist bases" and were in response to recent terrorist acts. The operation aimed to counter threats originating from Afghan territory.

item.title: Number of Pensioners Receiving Below Minimum Pension in Kyrgyzstan Decreases
item.description: In 2025, the minimum pension in Kyrgyzstan was set at 7,100 soms. However, 37 percent of pensioners were receiving less than this amount. Recent data indicates a decrease in the number of pensioners falling into this category.

item.title: Transformations in Karakalpakstan Aim for Human Dignity and Honor
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's recent visit to Karakalpakstan assessed transformations initiated in 2017. State policy focuses on expanding citizens' opportunities through new enterprises, healthcare, and education. Economic development is linked to social problem-solving and future confidence, addressing issues like Aral Sea consequences, soil salinization, and migration pressures.

item.title: Tajikistan's Petroglyphs Included in UNESCO Preliminary List
item.description: Five petroglyph complexes in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan region and four historical-natural sites in Khatlon region are now on UNESCO's Preliminary World Heritage List. The Agency for Protection of Historical and Cultural Heritage stated these sites represent valuable historical and cultural heritage, crucial for studying ancient civilizations and regional development.

item.title: Uzbekistan explores participation in Nakhichevan railway construction project
item.description: Uzbekistan is exploring the possibility of participating in the construction of the Nakhichevan railway, a project that would provide access to Turkey's Samsun and Istanbul ports. This initiative is part of a broader strategy to make Uzbekistan a key link in the shortest land route from the Pacific to Europe, aiming to double transport services by 2030.

item.title: China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway construction to expand, impacting regional trade
item.description: Construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway is set to expand, a development expected to alter the region's map and reduce import costs. This infrastructure project holds significant importance for Tajikistan, potentially facilitating cheaper trade and improved connectivity.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans 17 New Logistics Centers and Terminals
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to establish 17 new logistics centers and terminals. These projects are slated for implementation in Tashkent city and the Tashkent, Andijan, Surxondaryo, and Buxoro regions, according to a meeting chaired by the President.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Invest $200 Million in Railway Modernization
item.description: Uzbekistan may allocate $200 million for railway modernization. The funds are intended to increase the capacity of the Maktaaral-Sirdaryo, Angren-Pop, Toshguzor-Boysun-Qumkurgan, Tashkent-Samarkand, and Toqimachi-Angren sections by 25-30%.

item.title: Tajikistan Presents "One Health" Approach at FAO Global Conference
item.description: Tajikistan shared its national experience in food security and sustainable production systems at the FAO Global Conference on "One Health" in agro-food systems in Rome. The conference, held September 21-23, focuses on practical applications of the "One Health" approach to enhance food security and resilience.

item.title: UN Warns of Mass Displacement Due to Sea Level Rise by Century's End
item.description: The United Nations warns that a potential half-meter rise in sea levels by the end of the century could force between 150 to 300 million people to leave their homes. Scientists have not ruled out this scenario, highlighting the significant threat of climate change-induced displacement.

item.title: Four Arrested in Tashkent Region for Operating Drug Laboratory in Rented Apartment
item.description: Four individuals were apprehended in Chirchiq, Tashkent region, for allegedly operating a drug laboratory in a rented apartment to produce and sell narcotics. The State Security Service reported the operation involved processing hashish oil and semi-finished products.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Implements New Registration Rules for Foreigners and Stateless Persons
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has updated its registration procedures for foreigners and stateless individuals. The new rules aim to streamline registration, clarify document and accommodation requirements, and establish uniform standards for various foreign national categories. Registration must occur after entry and by the last day of permitted stay without prior registration.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's security service disrupts Afghan hashish smuggling route via Tajikistan
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (SCNS) has successfully disrupted a transnational drug trafficking route. The route was used to smuggle hashish originating from Afghanistan through Tajikistan and into Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Uzbekistan Official Explains New Party Registration Process and Government Reforms
item.description: Tohirjon Safarov, deputy head of the Agency for Strategic Development and Reforms, clarified issues concerning the registration of new parties and initiative groups. He also addressed government downsizing and the opening timeline for the Public Chamber.

item.title: Earthquake in Tajikistan Felt in Uzbekistan's Fergana Valley with Intensity of 2 Points
item.description: An earthquake originating in Tajikistan on September 21 registered a magnitude of 4.9 with a depth of 160 km. The tremors were felt in Uzbekistan's Fergana region, including Sokh, Quvasoy, and Fergana districts, with an intensity of 2 points.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank: Banks have significant buffer despite deposit outflow
item.description: Banks in Kyrgyzstan experienced a deposit outflow of 24.5 billion soms in one month. The National Bank stated that financial institutions have built a substantial buffer. Despite monthly fluctuations, the deposit base grew 3.9% year-on-year.

item.title: Almalyk Mining and Metallurgical Company receives Ba2 credit rating from Moody's
item.description: The Almalyk Mining and Metallurgical Company (AMMC) has obtained a credit rating of "Ba2" with a "Stable" outlook from Moody's. AMMC also received an independent credit assessment (BCA) of "ba3".
